findings.description: AWS access key and secret key are embedded in plaintext within the instance user_data script, which is visible to anyone with EC2 API access or console access to the instance metadata, and stored unencrypted in the Terraform state and AMI logs.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH management access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0 with no compensating controls (e.g., WAF), broadening the attack surface for the web application to the entire internet.
The security group's egress rule allows all outbound traffic (protocol -1) to 0.0.0.0/0, which can facilitate data exfiltration if the instance is compromised.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true (it is commented out), so data stored on the volume is unencrypted at rest, risking exposure if the underlying storage is accessed improperly.
The EBS snapshot inherits encryption status from the unencrypted source volume, meaning the snapshot data is also unencrypted and could be exposed if shared or accessed by unauthorized parties.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, increasing direct internet exposure of hosted resources.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, increasing direct internet exposure of hosted resources.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket used for VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, potentially exposing sensitive network flow log data.

force_destroy = true combined with no bucket policy or access controls could allow logs to be permanently deleted, and the lack of restriction may allow unauthorized read/write access to sensitive flow logs.
